body: Investigated 2026-07-12 (WIP explored + codex-reviewed, then reverted; commit 9bdc7e09 dropped, nothing wired to production). ROOT BLOCKER (codex CHANGES-REQUESTED, confirmed against code): the seal hot path (segmented.rs ~1223-1235) is deliberately O(1) — it does NOT list/read the manifest tail per seal ('the normal single-writer hot path must not list the manifest before every seal'); it trusts an in-memory cached next_manifest_index/committed_epoch. Consequently the ONLY cross-owner fence for a stale/superseded writer is the put_if_absent INDEX COLLISION on the write-once manifest/{index}.json address space: a stale writer's cached index is already occupied -> CAS fails -> it re-reads -> observes the newer epoch -> self-fences (EpochFenced). PHYSICAL compaction that DELETES a below-floor index FREES that address, so a writer dormant longer than the retention window can wake, WIN put_if_absent at the freed index, and FALSE-ACK a phantom entry below the live epoch tail that tail-only recover_manifest never replays (lost write / split-brain ack). So 'delete below-floor low indices is index-disjoint from every append' is FALSE for a stale cached-index writer — disjointness holds only for a writer at the TRUE tail. DECISION (Erik, 2026-07-12): DEFER — do not ship delete-only; this bead must FIRST decide the hot-path/CAS design. Two viable directions: (a) TAIL-VALIDATE the CAS write paths (seal/acquire_epoch/advance_retention_floor re-read the tail after a put_if_absent WIN and reject a resurrected below-tail hole via rollback+EpochFenced) — correct but REGRESSES the deliberate O(1) TD-004 group-commit seal (adds a LIST per seal); or (b) a NON-INDEX-REUSING scheme (generation/namespace rewrite with an atomic current-generation pointer, or mark-dead markers that keep indices occupied) — mark-dead keeps O(1) seal + CAS-safety but does NOT bound per-read LIST cost (only storage bytes), so it fails acceptance #1; a generation rewrite bounds both but is a large addressing/recovery change and still needs a hot-path current-generation check to prevent the stale-writer false-ack. SECONDARY codex findings to fold in when implemented: (i) read coherence needs a BlobStore LIST-consistency contract (LocalFsBlobStore::list is a non-snapshot read_dir); (ii) empty-seed-tail branch edge (cut at f+1 when source floor f is the last record makes recover_manifest derive next-seq f -> first append acks at seq f which the sub-floor read filter hides) — reject such cuts or seed next-seq at f+1. The read-path hardening explored in the reverted WIP (explicit floor fail-closed, straddling-segment exclusive-lower-bound, genesis-seed vs reclamation-floor discriminator) is sound + behavior-preserving and can be re-derived here. This is a pre-existing SLOW space/latency leak (manifest grows with commands on long-lived trimmed queues), NOT a regression; deferring keeps the status quo.
summary: BLOCKED: delete-only compaction breaks manifest-CAS write-once fence; needs hot-path/CAS design decision before implementation

body: Design doc: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md (+ codex stress-test corrections in section 6). Q1: writer staleness effectively UNBOUNDED at the segmented.rs substrate (no TTL forces a manifest re-read; the only stale-writer fence is the put_if_absent index collision on the write-once address space; the ~15s CP lease lives in a layer the substrate is designed not to trust and doesn't survive a GC-pause-between-resolve-and-CAS or the raw path). Q2: delete-only unsafe (no proven staleness bound W, no enforced retention>W invariant). codex REFUTED D-B tail-validate (a legitimate winner at index I whose peer builds I+1 gets its valid entry mis-deleted; rollback can delete a branch-pinned shared segment; not crash-safe). RECOMMENDATION (Option 1): add BlobStore::list_from(prefix,start_after) (S3-native StartAfter; trivial for InMemory/LocalFs) + a durable monotonic compacted_through_index watermark advanced only below the epoch-fenced floor; recover_manifest/read_manifest range-list from W -> O(live) LIST+GET, fully bounding per-read cost; keep all indices OCCUPIED so the fence + O(1) seal are unchanged and no stale-writer false-ack is possible; optional mark-dead shrinks per-entry bytes. Residual: object COUNT grows as tiny never-read markers (price of the write-once fence); fully bounding storage count needs Option 2 (redesigned fencing/commit protocol: permanent head object + CAS + unique per-attempt segment keys) — high blast radius, only if tiny-marker growth is unacceptable. Awaiting Erik's Option 1 vs Option 2 decision before implementing.
summary: Design analysis complete + codex-verified: staleness UNBOUNDED at substrate; delete-only + D-B tail-validate both unsafe; recommend RANGE-LIST(start_after)+watermark, zero hot-path change, bounds read cost

body: Commit 9317c3c9 on top of v0.13.0 (crates/pqueue-objectlog only). Bounds per-READ cost via a durable monotonic read-horizon watermark + a BlobStore::list_from(prefix,start_after) primitive (S3-native StartAfter, >1000-key pagination-correct; default filter-after-list for InMemory/LocalFs). Horizon stored at {shard}read_horizon.json (outside manifest/), advanced at the END of expire_segments_through across the oldest contiguous prefix of provably-reclaimed below-floor entries, bounded by reclaimed_through (not floor) so a partial expire never hides an undeleted segment; stops below the authoritative floor entry, live/not-yet-reclaimed data, branch-pinned below-floor segments, and the tail; monotonic. recover_manifest + read_manifest range-list from the horizon (tail=max, defensive full-list fallback, backward-compat when no horizon object). Re-added the sound floor fail-closed in read_all/read_from_limited (from_seq<=floor -> EngineError::Storage; floor+1 succeeds), gated on a horizon existing so a branch seq==f genesis seed is not suppressed; TOCTOU closed by capturing the horizon ONCE and driving both the guard and the enumeration from that snapshot. FENCE PROVABLY UNTOUCHED: below-horizon manifest addresses are never freed (no delete/rename/mark) -> put_if_absent still collides -> stale writer still EpochFenced; test stale_writer_below_horizon_is_still_fenced_address_never_freed asserts the below-horizon object still exists AND the stale writer gets EpochFenced. Seal hot path byte-identical to v0.13.0 (diff-confirmed, no list/get before the CAS). ACCEPTED residual (Erik's decision, read-cost-only): object COUNT/bytes still grow slowly as never-read below-horizon entries; fully bounding COUNT would need the fencing/commit-protocol redesign (design doc Option 2), not pursued. codex: round1 REJECT (read TOCTOU, W-monotonicity, partial-expire leak, billable undercount) -> all fixed -> round2 APPROVE. Verify (1.92.0): objectlog substrate 42/42; full workspace test exit 0; fmt clean; clippy -D warnings clean. Design record: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md.
summary: Implemented Option 1 (read-horizon watermark + range-list); codex APPROVE round 2; fence untouched, O(1) seal unchanged, read cost bounded to live
